title: Define the state
prompt: For House Robber (rob non-adjacent houses, maximize loot), the right meaning for `dp[i]` is…
options: The maximum loot obtainable from houses 0..i (whether or not house i itself is robbed)
The number of ways to rob i houses
explanation: With that meaning the recurrence follows directly: skip house i (dp[i-1]) or rob it, which forbids i-1 (dp[i-2] + nums[i]), and take the max. 'Whether house i is robbed' isn't a number you can optimize, and 'the loot in house i' is just the input.

title: Drill: space-optimized DP
prompt: From memory: tribonacci — T(0)=0, T(1)=1, T(2)=1, then T(n) = T(n-1)+T(n-2)+T(n-3). Return T(n) using THREE rolling variables, no array. (n ≤ 37, fits in int.)

solution.explanation: Handle the bases first, then compute and shift every variable one slot left. Assign `a = b` before `b = c`, or you'll overwrite a value you still need. O(n) time, O(1) space.

hints: T(n) depends on only the previous three values. How many values do you actually need to keep?
Return early for n = 0, 1, 2. Then keep `a, b, c` = T(i-3), T(i-2), T(i-1) and loop i from 3 to n.
Inside the loop: `int cur = a + b + c; a = b; b = c; c = cur;`

title: Drill: max non-adjacent sum
prompt: From memory (rolling DP): return the maximum sum of elements of `nums` such that no two chosen elements are adjacent. Use two rolling variables, no array.

solution.explanation: At each element, either skip it (keep the best so far) or take it (best from two back + x). Starting both variables at 0 handles empty and one-element inputs with no special case. O(n) time, O(1) space.

hints: For the current element you have exactly two choices. What does each choice rule out?
best(i) = max(best(i-1), best(i-2) + nums[i]). Only the last two bests matter.
`int cur = Math.max(prev1, prev2 + x); prev2 = prev1; prev1 = cur;`

title: Drill: fewest perfect squares
prompt:
From memory (state = amount): return the fewest perfect squares (1, 4, 9, 16, …) that sum to `n`.

`12` → `3` (4 + 4 + 4), `13` → `2` (4 + 9). `1 <= n <= 10⁴`.

solution.explanation: This is Coin Change where the coins are the perfect squares. The last square used leaves an amount whose best answer is already in the table. Since 1 is a square, every amount is reachable. O(n·√n) time, O(n) space.

hints: This is Coin Change in disguise. What are the 'coins'?
dp[a] = fewest squares summing to a. dp[0] = 0, and fill the rest with a sentinel.
`for (int s = 1; s * s <= a; s++) dp[a] = Math.min(dp[a], dp[a - s * s] + 1);`

title: Recall: 0/1 subset sum
prompt: Fill in the boolean subset-sum loop: can some subset of `nums` (each used at most once) sum to `target`?
explanation: The empty subset makes sum 0, so `dp[0] = true`. For each number, go from `target` down to `x`. Sum `j` becomes reachable if `j - x` was reachable *before* this number, and going downwards guarantees you're reading those older values.

title: Forwards instead?
prompt: In the 1-D subset-sum loop, you change `for (int j = target; j >= x; j--)` to `for (int j = x; j <= target; j++)`. What happens?
options: Each number can be used multiple times: dp[j - x] may already include x from earlier in the same pass, so it becomes an unbounded knapsack
Nothing; the order of j never matters
Some reachable sums are missed, so it returns false too often
explanation: Going forwards, `dp[j - x]` may have just become true because of this same `x`, so `dp[j]` counts x twice. With `nums = [5]` and target 10, forwards sets dp[5] and then dp[10], which is wrong. Backwards reads only values from before this number. The forwards order is exactly right for unbounded problems like Coin Change, where coins can be reused.

title: Recall: expand around center
prompt: Fill in Longest Palindromic Substring by expanding around every odd and even center.
explanation: `(i, i)` is the odd center and `(i, i + 1)` is the even center. When the loop stops, `l` and `r` are one step past the palindrome on each side, so its length is `r - l - 1`. From center `i`, the palindrome starts `(len - 1) / 2` characters to the left, and integer division makes that work for both odd and even lengths.
